steps.title: Three different note names
steps.body:
**triad** means a chord made from three different note names arranged with alternate notes of a scale. C, E and G make a triad: in the C major scale, choose C, skip D, choose E, skip F, choose G.

**Why it matters:** A guitar can sound six strings but still have only three different note names, because some notes repeat.

steps.title: Read and hear the notes
steps.body: C, E, G are three different names. Playing another C an octave higher repeats a name; it does not add a fourth kind of note.

items.prompt: Play C, E, G together. Use any positions for these notes.

steps.title: Make it familiar
steps.body: Play C, E and G together. Then try C at string 2 fret 1 instead of string 5 fret 3. The check accepts either octave.
